description: v2.1.0 section 22 lists ParticipationPolicyDef as a Definition Layer object, but section 15 only spells out the runtime ParticipationResult type (15.4) and the general mode/basis distinctions (15.1-15.3). JUDGMENT CALL (flagged for review): modeled here as the definition-time counterpart of 15.4 — for each participation mode available on an offense, it declares the attribution/dependency basis and, for derivative modes, the typed conclusion_type the principal must have reached (section 15.3/15.4's 'Instigation requires OffenseRealization<X>, not LiabilityResult<X>' point). The runtime type checker (step 2) is what actually raises the TYPE ERROR shown in section 15.4 when the required conclusion is unavailable; this schema only records what to check.

attributable_slots.description: Which of this offense's elements slots can be satisfied via ATTRIBUTE(other co-principal's conduct) rather than this actor's own conduct — section 15.2's example attributes property_taking(by=乙) to 甲 and violence(by=甲) to 乙, both under 'conduct'.

requires_conclusion.description: Section 15.3: the principal's personal culpability defenses do not defeat this dependency, so the required level is typically offense_realization, not offense_establishment or liability_result — but this is left offense-specific rather than hardcoded, since section 15 does not universally mandate one level for every derivative mode.
